minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved counsel's responses to two Open Meeting Law complaints and passed the FY19 budget.
minutes.summary: Town counsel walked the commission through draft responses to two Open Meeting Law complaints, finding forwarded emails technically a violation and some minutes approved late, and the commission approved both responses. It then raised the capital reserve transfer, approved the FY19 budget, removed a warrant article, amended minutes, and reviewed proposed Charter changes before entering executive session on Highfield Village litigation.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission approved town counsel's draft responses to two Open Meeting Law complaints, the second as modified.
Counsel found forwarded emails technically a violation and some minutes approved late; remedial action on the emails was discussed.
The commission raised the transfer into the capital reserve account and approved the FY19 budget with that change.
Warrant article 5 is to be removed or passed over, and stabilization fund transfers move to fall town meeting.
A special meeting on the Sewer Commission Charter is to be called, and a financial policy is to go on a future agenda.

why_it_matters: The FY19 sewer budget sets what the sewer system collects and sets aside, and it leaned on one-time connection fees, which do not recur in later years' rates.
Money moved out of the capacity stabilization fund is to come back at fall town meeting, so residents will be asked to vote on that transfer.
watch_next: A special meeting at 7:00 pm on April 3 at the DPW to review the Sewer Commission Charter sections.
A future agenda item on financial policy, with grease traps, billing and irrigation meters also requested.
